subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should gh-issues unattended worker hardening require a runtime untrusted-content boundary plus per-spawn child tool scoping before this issue can close?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent fix defines a security/API boundary across prompt-defined skills, sessions_spawn tool policy, sandbox requirements, child session state, and SECURITY.md hardening-versus-vulnerability semantics.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and tool scoping
options.body: Land or replace the toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent isolation before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept prompt-only hardening
options.body: Treat prompt guidance and current global subagent policy as enough defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain inside the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer to unified delegation design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers design one delegated-agent content and capability policy covering skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and tool scoping
recommendation.body: Land or replace the toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent isolation before closing this issue.
